prompts: The investors meet tomorrow and want the first half of 2026 closed. The books and the board's notes are in {WS}/finance. How did each month go, and how many months of cash do we have left at the current burn? Prepare what the CFO needs to present. Record the key figures in {WS}/result.json: revenue, gross_margin_pct and ebitda, each mapping 2026-01 to 2026-06 to its value, plus burn and runway_months.
answers:
## [goal] H1 2026 investor close

**Revenue reached R$1.39 million at a 70.24% gross margin. EBITDA was negative R$1.22 million.** June had the highest revenue and gross margin and the smallest EBITDA loss of the half.

**June 30 cash of R$1,847,350.40 covered 9.36 months at the board-defined burn of R$197,288.23 per month.** June 30 is the latest cash date in the books, so this estimate is measured from that date. :codex-file-citation{path="<WORKSPACE>/finance/cash_balance.txt" purpose="source"} :codex-file-citation{path="<WORKSPACE>/finance/README.md" purpose="source"}

## [action] Close basis

Grouped ledger entries by posting month and mapped them to the chart of accounts. Revenue includes refunds as reductions. Gross margin is gross profit divided by net revenue. EBITDA deducts sales and marketing, R&D, and G&A from gross profit and excludes financial income and expenses. The H1 margin uses H1 gross profit divided by H1 revenue. :codex-file-citation{path="<WORKSPACE>/finance/ledger.csv" purpose="source"} :codex-file-citation{path="<WORKSPACE>/finance/chart_of_accounts.csv" purpose="source"}

## [result] Monthly performance

| Month | Net revenue | Gross margin | EBITDA | What changed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Jan | R$200,510.87 | 70.03% | −R$210,278.96 | Lowest revenue of the half |
| Feb | R$216,328.06 | 70.29% | −R$212,300.08 | Higher R&D spend contributed to the widest loss |
| Mar | R$219,066.17 | 68.46% | −R$204,525.45 | Refunds and higher COGS pushed margin to its H1 low |
| Apr | R$238,163.26 | 70.24% | −R$196,950.65 | Gross profit recovered and the loss narrowed |
| May | R$243,032.89 | 69.56% | −R$201,945.82 | Higher R&D spend helped widen the loss |
| Jun | R$272,391.57 | 72.41% | −R$192,968.22 | Highest revenue and margin, smallest loss |
| **H1** | **R$1,389,492.82** | **70.24%** | **−R$1,218,969.18** | |

The board’s burn is the average EBITDA loss for April through June. Runway assumes that rate holds. Cash fell **R$461,837.60** from May to June, so the board should see that cash movement alongside the EBITDA-based estimate. The supplied books contain no cash-flow bridge for the difference.

## [next] Investor handoff

Use the table and runway estimate for the H1 presentation. Refresh the cash balance and trailing three-month EBITDA before quoting runway as of the meeting date.

The figures are saved in [result.json](<WORKSPACE>/result.json). The ledger rollup and a separate recalculation returned:

> Ledger reconciliation PASS: 86 entries across 6 months, all accounts mapped  
> Independent check PASS: 18 monthly metrics, burn and runway match result.json.
